title: PowerPoint on Mac: Copilot Agent Mode creates presentations from Work IQ
summary: The roadmap facts, licence assignment controls and published Work IQ statements are supported. Clarify that the Windows release note describes a separate roadmap item, and that the low cost rating concerns users who already hold the Copilot add-on licence.

claims.claim: Agent Mode in PowerPoint creates presentations from Work IQ without users having to find the relevant files, meetings and emails themselves.
claims.quote: Now with Agent Mode in PowerPoint, you can create presentations based on your Work IQ. Build rich presentations without the heavy lift of finding all the right files, meetings, and emails to compose relevant slides.

claims.claim: The products are PowerPoint and Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).

claims.claim: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer enabling agents to access and reason over organizational and business data.

claims.quote:
July 01, 2026

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The release notes say Copilot in PowerPoint uses Work IQ to gather files, meetings and emails for presentations.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint now uses Work IQ to automatically gather relevant files, meetings, and emails to help build presentations.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Open questions; front matter: changes
claims.claim: The named release-note entry is tagged Windows and does not list Mac, which the briefing describes as a platform disagreement.
claims.quote:
Create presentations with Work IQ using Agent Mode in Copilot in PowerPoint [Windows]
Roadmap ID: 555874
claims.fix: Replace the sentences beginning 'A Microsoft 365 Copilot release-notes entry' through 'follows the roadmap record for Mac' with: 'The Microsoft 365 Copilot release notes dated 1 July 2026 describe the Windows counterpart, roadmap item 555874, under "Create presentations with Work IQ using Agent Mode in Copilot in PowerPoint". That entry says Work IQ gathers relevant files, meetings and emails to help build presentations; it does not confirm the Mac implementation described by roadmap item 555872.' In the second Open question, replace 'given that the release-notes entry is tagged [Windows]' with 'given that the release notes describe the Windows counterpart'.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no page specifically describing this Work IQ presentation capability on Mac at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Work IQ Mac Agent'; 'PowerPoint Agent Mode Mac create presentations'. Read release notes and search excerpts for Office Document Tools, Office for Mac and Work IQ; none describes this Mac capability.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The default state of this Mac capability is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Work IQ default'; 'PowerPoint Mac Agent Mode create presentations Work IQ default admin disable setting license Basic'. Read roadmap, release-note entry, Copilot overview and Work IQ enablement; none states this feature's default.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether an administrator must enable this Mac capability or act on its arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Agent Mode disable admin'; 'PowerPoint Mac Agent Mode create presentations Work IQ default admin disable setting license Basic'. Read roadmap, release-note entry, Copilot overview and Work IQ enablement; no feature-specific admin action is stated.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record gives no rollout mechanics.
claims.quote: Searched: Read the complete supplied roadmap record for rollout mechanics, channels and deployment instructions. It gives status, target date, phase and platform, but no rollout procedure.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record gives no prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: Read the complete supplied roadmap record for prerequisites and enablement requirements. Neither its description nor its fields lists prerequisites.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ actions run in a specific user's context and access only what that user is allowed to see or do.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: The release-note entry says the integration accesses only authorized content.
claims.quote: This integration reduces manual effort and improves content relevance while maintaining data security by accessing only authorized content.

claims.claim: The roadmap record does not state where generated presentations are saved.
claims.quote: Searched: Read the complete supplied roadmap record for save location and storage. Its description covers presentation creation and content gathering, not where the output is saved.

claims.claim: The roadmap record does not state which source sensitivity labels a presentation inherits.
claims.quote: Searched: Read the complete supplied roadmap record for sensitivity labels and inheritance. It contains no statement about labels.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the relevant release-note entry describes a separate identity for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Read complete roadmap record and Work IQ presentation release-note entry for identity, service accounts and principals; neither describes a separate identity. The Work IQ overview instead describes user-scoped actions.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes content gathering and slide composition, but not sending or sharing presentations.
claims.quote: Searched: Read the complete supplied roadmap description for send, share and publish operations. It describes finding files, meetings and emails to compose slides, with no sending or sharing operation.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot's add-on licence provides the full Copilot experience in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Work IQ and work-data grounding are included in the Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) experience, supporting the included model for this option inside that licensed product.
claims.quote: Although both use the Work IQ platform, Work IQ is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), whereas the Work IQ API is a distinct usage-based billing offering

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: The overview's comparison table describes web-data-only Copilot Chat in both Basic columns and web and work data in the Premium column.
claims.quote: Securely interact with Copilot Chat using web data only | Securely interact with Copilot Chat using web data only | Securely interact with Copilot using web data and work data (Microsoft Graph and Work IQ)

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview says Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents for Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents.

claims.claim: The Work IQ overview states that custom and third-party agents are subject to usage-based billing.
claims.quote: It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap record names no meter or price for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Read the complete supplied roadmap record for meter, credits, billing and price. Its description and fields contain no meter or price.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Not yet published; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence or credit rule specific to Work IQ presentation creation in Agent Mode on Mac is published in the documentation checked.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Work IQ license'; 'PowerPoint Agent Mode Work IQ Mac licensing Copilot credits price prerequisites'. Read Copilot overview, Work IQ overview, release notes and Work IQ API enablement; only general product and API rules are stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not specifically establish whether Basic users can use this Work IQ option in Agent Mode on Mac.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Mac Agent Mode create presentations Work IQ default admin disable setting license Basic'. Read Copilot overview and Work IQ overview: Basic has in-app features and pay-as-you-go agents, but this Mac option is not identified.

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses reaches the user's licence controls.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign, then select Save changes.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the selected licence to a user using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: The two licence assignment pages do not mention this Work IQ presentation feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Read both cited licence assignment pages in full for Work IQ, Agent Mode and PowerPoint presentation creation. Neither page mentions this feature; both describe general Microsoft 365 licence assignment.

claims.claim: User licence assignment controls who holds the Copilot licence, indirectly governing access to the full Copilot experience rather than switching this capability itself.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The licence assignment page points to group-based licensing as another route.
claims.quote: To use group-based licensing, see Assign licenses to users by group membership in Microsoft Entra ID

claims.claim: The briefing rates this included capability's cost low, while its rationale also calls the existing Copilot add-on licence a known cost.
claims.quote: Work IQ is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), whereas the Work IQ API is a distinct usage-based billing offering
claims.fix: Keep cost low for the existing licensed audience, but replace the cost rationale with: 'Low. For users who already hold Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), Work IQ is included; the known incremental costs of this change are admin review and user communication. A licence or credit rule specific to this Mac capability is not yet published.' This distinguishes the existing product licence from the incremental cost of the change.
